Eternal Night

Where nobody looks anymore, the night stays.

Not every part of the city gets looked at. Sealed doors, empty windows, a sign for a shop that closed years ago, a painting on a wall nobody walks past anymore. Where attention has withdrawn, the night stays, even at noon. This is the Eternal Night. It is not a place so much as a condition, and it is the one thing Terminal City works against. Not a villain. Just forgetting. When people stop noticing a room, a wall, a habit a neighbourhood had, the night settles into it and what was there goes missing, quietly. The Eternal Night keeps nothing. It only shows the city where it is losing.

An ordinary photographer is trying to make a picture of an old painted sign before the first evening light goes. In every image, one edge falls into a loading-door shadow deeper than it looks to the eye. She steps back until the sign fits, then notices the faded lettering no longer draws anyone’s glance. A crow lands on the lip of the shadow and shifts away. The photographer lowers the camera when the room host comes down the lane carrying a chair. Together they pause to look at the sign instead of its image. Nothing brightens dramatically. One worn corner is simply visible a little longer than before. The photographer takes a final picture and leaves. The shadow remains; attention has returned to one small part of its edge.

The ruleWhat nobody looks at is where the night lives.

Terminal City · Storybook v0.10.0 · built 2026-09-13
Terminal City is an original fictional mythology inspired by Vancouver’s geography, weather, wildlife, infrastructure, art, and electronic music. It makes no claim to historical, Indigenous, or religious tradition. Real places are used as settings; the operating system layered on them is invented.
Made by Steve Hiehn, a software developer and electronic musician based in Vancouver, Canada. All music was created using a custom DAW, Signals & Sorcery.
